notes:
Summary: Mariner is evaluating Redwood Dedicated to run low-latency real-time assistants for trading desk workflows and compliance reranking. Primary focus: define unambiguous latency SLOs and align measurement across Redwood, Mariner client, and infra teams.

Key constraints / asks (shorthand):
- SLO targets: want p50/p95/p99 table per route. Initial ask: p95 <= 100ms for non-streaming short responses (<=128 tokens); p99 <=250ms. For streaming chat they want first-token p95 <= 80ms, subsequent-token p95 <= 30ms.
- Throughput: baseline 200 RPS sustained, 600 RPS burst for market open — dedicated pool sizing required.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer reserved monthly commit with overage bursts; target ARR range aligns with forecast.
- Security: VPC peering, KMS-managed keys, SOC2 attestation, audit log retention 3 years, SSO via SAML + SCIM provisioning.

Measurement alignment discussion (detailed snippets / CRM-style notes):
- "Who measures p95?" — Mariner SRE wants client-side measurement (browser/edge) for end-to-end SLA. Redwood argues server-side and ingress-egress markers are necessary to isolate infra latency. Need exact wiring: timestamps at client send, Redwood ingress, model token emit, Redwood egress, client receive.
- Agreement proposal: publish both server-side (Redwood ingress->egress) and normalized client-side (client send->client receive) numbers. For contractual SLA use server-side p95 with clearly listed exclusions (network ISP variance, client throttling).
- Streaming vs non-streaming: Must define first-byte vs last-byte latencies. Mariner flatly stated: "first token matters for perceived latency". Proposal: SLOs include two separate metrics per route: first-token p95 and steady-state per-token median/p95.
- Measurement windows and retention: 5-minute sliding windows for alerting; 30-day aggregated histograms for reporting; raw traces stored for 90 days.
- Sampling & instrumentation: Use deterministic trace-ids in headers to correlate client traces with Redwood request ids. Add a synthetic steady-state traffic generator during POC to validate p99 tail under load.
- Calculation rules: define RPC timeout, retry behavior, and how to treat partial responses (stream aborted) for SLO math. Example rule: aborted streams counted as failures; time-to-first-byte recorded but route marked degraded.

POC scope and acceptance criteria (short):
- 2-week dedicated POC in us-west with reserved 8xA100 equivalent capacity.
- Synthetic workload driver: mixed chat+rerank at configured RPS and token lengths.
- Success: observed server-side p95 <= 100ms for non-streaming, first-token streaming p95 <= 80ms, and system does not exceed error budget (2% p95 breaches) over 72-hour steady-state run.

Quotes / client language (verbatim-ish):
- "If the first token is slow, traders lose confidence — that perception is everything." — Head of Trading Automation, Mariner.
- "We need the SLA to reflect what we actually measure in production, not just what the cloud console shows." — SRE lead.

Next steps (owner-level):
- AE (Lena) to circulate updated SLO worksheet with explicit timing marker definitions (client-send, ingress, model-emit, egress, client-receive) by 2026-03-11.
- SE (Ravi) to spin up POC plan and cost estimates; confirm NFRs for audit logs by 2026-03-14.
